summary_corrections.primitive-roots-and-unit-groups-modulo-n:
The published unit group $(\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z)^\times$ collects the residue classes coprime to $n$, the unit criterion recognises them, and Euler's totient counts them. The order of a group element, its characterisation by which powers are trivial, and the fact that it divides the order of the group constrain every generator argument. The Chinese remainder theorem splits $\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z$ along a prime factorisation, $\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z$ is a field, a finite subgroup of the units of an integral domain is cyclic, and the solvability and solution count of a linear congruence are known. Coprimality, least common multiples and the $p$-adic valuation supply the remaining arithmetic.

A primitive root modulo $n$ is a generator of the unit group, and the index relative to a chosen generator converts multiplication into addition modulo $\varphi(n)$. Cyclicity of the unit group of a prime field yields primitive roots modulo a prime, Euler's criterion for the solvability of $x^m\equiv a$, and the exact number of its solution classes. The page then lifts a primitive root from $p$ to every odd prime power and determines the exceptional structure $(\mathbb Z/2^k\mathbb Z)^\times\cong C_2\times C_{2^{k-2}}$ for $k\ge3$. The Chinese remainder decomposition assembles the prime-power factors into the structure of the unit group modulo any $n$, and from it the page derives the Carmichael function and its formula, classifies the moduli $1,2,4,p^k,2p^k$ admitting primitive roots, and counts them.
summary_corrections.semidirect-products-and-automorphism-gro:
Group actions, their correspondence with homomorphisms into a symmetric group, normal subgroups, quotient groups and the first isomorphism theorem are the published setting for an extension. Conjugation by a fixed element is an automorphism, the inner automorphisms form a normal subgroup of the automorphism group, and a characteristic subgroup is one carried to itself by every automorphism. Lagrange's theorem, Cauchy's theorem for finite groups, the classification of cyclic groups, the unit criterion modulo $n$, the field $\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z$, the root bound for a polynomial over an integral domain and the free abelian group of finite rank supply the arithmetic the later sections use.

An action of $H$ on $N$ by automorphisms twists the direct-product law into the external semidirect product $N\rtimes H$. The page proves it is a group, identifies its canonical normal factor and complement, and shows the product is direct exactly when the action is trivial; the internal recognition theorem and the splitting lemma then match a homomorphic section, a complement to the kernel, and a semidirect-product decomposition. The automorphism side defines the outer automorphism group, proves a characteristic subgroup of a normal subgroup is normal, and builds the holomorph with its faithful affine action and its recognition of regular normal subgroups. It computes $\operatorname{Aut}(C_n)$ and $\operatorname{Aut}(\mathbb Z^n)$, shows actions differing by an automorphism give isomorphic products, develops generalized and ordinary dihedral groups, and closes with the classification of groups of order $pq$.

summary_rationale.primitive-roots-and-unit-groups-modulo-n: Both failures are in the proposed text. (a) Paragraph 1 was entirely the page's own development — it opened with the page's own definition of a primitive root and continued "This page develops … proves … and carries …", so no background from the declared closure appeared anywhere. (b) The final sentence of paragraph 2 surveyed the companion page ("The companion page turns the structural results into generator tests, index tables, …"), which SCHEMA §6 forbids. The replacement puts the published unit group, unit criterion, totient, element order and its divisibility, the Chinese remainder theorem, the field Z/pZ, cyclicity of a finite subgroup of the units of a domain, and the linear-congruence count in paragraph 1, and confines paragraph 2 to this page's own progression.
summary_rationale.semidirect-products-and-automorphism-gro: Same two failures. Paragraph 1 opened "An action of H on N by automorphisms twists the direct-product law …" and then "This page proves the group law, identifies …" — the development, not the background; and paragraph 2 closed with a survey of the companion page ("The companion supplies affine, dihedral, symmetric, holomorph, … examples"). The replacement gives paragraph 1 the published group actions, normal subgroups and quotients, the first isomorphism theorem, conjugation as an automorphism, the inner automorphism group, characteristic subgroups, Lagrange, Cauchy, the classification of cyclic groups, the unit criterion, Z/pZ, the root bound over a domain and the free abelian group of finite rank — all of which the page's items actually cite — and keeps the development, including the item-17 isomorphism lemma the proposal mentioned only obliquely, in paragraph 2.
